block_05_direct_answer.title: Direct answer
block_05_direct_answer.body_html: Luxury fit depends on scarcity, quality and buyer relevance rather than price alone. For townhouse buyers, compare location, quality, scarcity, service level, charges, brand value where relevant and the depth of the future buyer pool. Treat premium positioning as one value component rather than proof of stronger returns, liquidity or resale.

items.answer: Luxury fit depends on scarcity, quality and buyer relevance rather than price alone. For townhouse buyers, compare the price premium with comparable non-branded or less premium alternatives instead of treating the brand as value by itself.
items.question: How should I assess whether a luxury property fits my needs?

items.answer: A branded residence is worthwhile only when the underlying property justifies the premium. Review service standards, management arrangements, recurring charges and owner obligations that come with the branded or luxury proposition.
items.question: How should I assess whether a branded residence fits my needs?

items.answer: End-user fit is mainly about how well the property supports everyday life. Confirm that the community provides the amenities, access and practical services needed now or within the buyer's realistic move-in timeline.
items.question: How should I assess whether a property suits an end-user buyer?

items.answer: Family fit depends on the home and the surrounding daily routine. Check whether the home can remain suitable if family size, work patterns or other practical needs change during ownership.
items.question: How should I assess whether a property suits a family buyer?

items.answer: A floor plan should be judged by usable space, not only total area. Corridors, awkward corners or oversized circulation reduce the usable value of the stated size. Compare plans at similar sizes because two units with the same area can function very differently.
